title: Breast self-exam
what: Once a month, you look at and feel your breasts yourself. This makes it easier to notice changes and see a doctor in time.
why: For all women, usually once a month. A self-exam does not replace a doctor's exam and a mammogram.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes once a month
tell_doctor: If the skin or nipple has changed
If there is discharge from the nipple
If breast cancer runs in your family

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Best 5 to 10 days after your period starts. If you have no periods, on the same day each month.

prepare.title: Place
prepare.text: In front of a mirror in good light, and lying down.

prepare.title: Habit
prepare.text: Set a reminder on your phone.

bring: A comfortable place to lie down
steps: Stand in front of a mirror with your arms down
Check if both breasts look the same in shape and skin
Raise your arms and look again
Lie on your back with one arm behind your head
With your finger pads, feel the breast in circles, from the edge to the nipple
Gently squeeze the nipple to check for discharge
feel: Breasts can feel uneven and a little lumpy. This is often normal
Before your period, your breasts may be more tender
after: Learn what your breasts usually feel like
If something has changed, make a doctor's appointment. Do not wait
Have doctor's exams and mammograms as advised for your age
red_flags: A new lump that does not go away after your period
Pulled-in skin or nipple, or skin that looks like orange peel

faq.q: If I find a lump, is it dangerous?
faq.a: Most lumps are not dangerous. But you must see a doctor.

faq.q: At what age should I start self-exams?
faq.a: Usually from age 20, or as soon as you can make it a habit.

reminders.text: Time for your monthly breast self-exam. It takes 5 to 10 minutes.
